newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Price stability essential to NZ strategy - Peters.
newsitem.headline: Price stability essential to NZ strategy - Peters.

text.p: New Zealand Treasurer Winston Peters said on Tuesday price stability was essential to the centre-right coalition government's strategy.
"Widening the inflation band to zero to three percent does not jeopardise that," he told a breakfast meeting of Wellington business men and women.
"Rather it enables the Reserve Bank to smoothly manage monetary policy."
He said although the Coalition Agreement signed in December between the National and New Zealand First Parties agreed extra spending, the boundaries were clear.
The government had deferred tax cuts for a year to ensure additional spending did not add to inflationary pressure.
"Despite all the precipitate language, the net fiscal change over previous plans for 1997/98 will be small, at most $200 million."
Peters said reducing public debt was a key priority for his government.
"Maintaining fiscal surpluses will enable further debt reduction and boost national savings."
New Zealand's economy had to be open and outward looking, he said.
The key to that was maintaining stable macroeconomic policies, deregulated, competitive and open markets, providing quality public services and having the lowest possible tax rates.
Peters said there were four core economic principles at the heart of the government's strategy.
* ensuring an economic climate conducive to sustainable development and growth
* an open, internationally competitive economy with a strong export sector,
* planning for the country's future, emphasising "intergenerational fairness" and increasing savings.
